status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Assess generative AI and agent systems for supply-chain, direct-prompt, indirect-prompt and connected-resource attacks.
review.reason_for_change: Weapon-themed text embedded in an artefact under GAI-assisted defensive inspection is a connected-resource/indirect-input attack design, materially relevant to assessment of such attacks. The Scott-Railton report preserves intent but no named scanner configuration or operational refusal on the specific sample; the related package demonstration is not this spyware execution path. Neither source preserves the platform's attack-assessment programme or its coverage of the reported tactic. Its outcome remains Boundary, independently of whether the reported attack succeeded.

conclusion_change.previous: The reported tactic aimed to make an AI-assisted defensive analysis stop on weapon-themed text embedded in the object under inspection. The record establishes an attempted attack on the inspection boundary, while the available occurrence evidence does not establish that a defined safeguard actually activated without its valid trigger or that malware passed a scanner. A canonical control-activation failure is therefore unresolved. The source-clause disposition remains resolved-no-mapping for this reported attempt. Intent to induce refusal is not an observed control activation, and related demonstrations do not substitute for this missing occurrence path. The fully adjudicated unclassified result does not assert the tactic is harmless or that any invariant held. No eligible or independently source-identified admitted external requirement is established; no external finding is asserted.
